chunks: And with this chain, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn 'Imran, from Ibn Mahbub, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Constantly wearing the leather sock (khuff) is a protection from leprosy. He said: I asked, 'In winter or in summer?' He said, 'Whether it is winter or summer.'

key_terms.الْخُفِّ: Leather sock (a type of footwear used in Islamic jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual or physical benefit of constantly wearing leather socks according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) linking the habitual wearing of *khuff* (leather socks) to physical protection from leprosy (*al-judham*), a condition often associated with impurity in Islamic jurisprudence. The Imam’s clarification that this benefit applies regardless of season underscores the continuous spiritual and physical merit of maintaining ritual purity through consistent attire, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between bodily habits and divine protection.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 2. And from the previous chain from Muhammad b. Ahmad from Musa b. ’Imran from Ibn Mahbub from Muawiyah b. Wahab from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said:
“A person who wears shoes often does not get involved in leprosy.” The narrator asked, “Are you talking about summer or winter?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “There is no difference between them.”
